whyThisShow: This is a strong mid-80s Nassau show with a first set that draws consistent praise — a rare Supplication Jam anchors it, and one reviewer called the first set "so kickin" before noting things soften after Drums. The Terrapin that opens the second set is a genuine highlight; one listener called it "a perfect version" with an extended jam after the shed light line. The show closes with a Johnny B. Goode that one reviewer called "blazing fast, the fastest version I've ever heard". One voice does flag that Jerry "does not sound himself" coming out of Space, so the second set has its rough patches. Unreleased, but the Oade Brothers AUD recording is regarded as excellent, and one listener noted the sound was "amazing" and the recording captures it.
listenFor: The Supplication Jam in the first set is the rare-treat centerpiece — one reviewer noted "great group improvisation" with Phil laying down "amazing lines under Jerry's fiery noodling". In the Terrapin, stay for the outro which develops into what one reviewer described as "a bouncy, lively Man Smart". The Bottom of the Bottle sequence features "a lot of group interplay and funky, bluesy soloing by Jerry" with Phil "prominent" as the jam peaks. Brent is consistently sharp throughout; one reviewer singled out his "great solos, especially Brent's hammond" in Minglewood and his "passionate singing and great soloing" on Baby, What You Want Me to Do. The second-set drop-off after Drums is real and noted by at least one listener, so temper expectations for the stretch from Space onward.
context: March 1985 was part of a spring tour that one reviewer noted had all general admission seating, lending an unusual floor energy to the Nassau run. The recording circulates as an Oade Brothers–transferred Schoeps AUD (identifier: gd85-03-29.oade-schoeps.sacks.23475.sbeok.flacf), which reviewers consistently praise for fidelity. The show remains officially unreleased, making the Archive.org AUD the primary way the community has kept it in circulation.
funFact: One reviewer described the Johnny B. Goode closing the show as "the equivalent of the horse galloping as it sees the barn" — the fastest version they'd encountered.
headline: Nassau's wild first set, March '85, Jerry cooking.
